body.name: Ranked fixing-overlap saturation handle
body.construction: Starting from \((G,\phi_G,\Omega_G)_{G\in\mathfrak R(H)}\), design a finite worklist saturation using \(\mathsf{Ops}\). Every reachable overlap state must satisfy the following invariant: its guards form a finite cover of every feasible pair \((G,p)\) retained from the initial family; on each guarded piece, every stored fixing kernel and arithmetic DAG equals the corresponding \(\phi_G(p)\) on \(\Omega_G\); each unresolved refinement pair records precisely the common-law cells not yet certified equal or separated; and every transition preserves covered feasible pairs and cannot discard a cell on which two retained target values disagree. A terminal positive state is encoded as the finite list \(((g_b,F_b))_{b=1}^m\), with guard coverage, positive-divisor annotations, and pairwise common-value identities sufficient for \(\operatorname{Eval}\). A terminal negative state is encoded as \((G_1,G_2,M_1,M_2,p,c_x,c_y)\) together with topological-order, exact-coarsening, response-table, latent-support, positivity, complete-law-equality, and target-separation checks, using integer-polynomial and isolating-interval encodings for real-algebraic entries. Derive a well-founded rank that strictly decreases after every nonterminal transition.
